svg.text: The verb: cut it fair
Set how many equal pieces, slice, give them out. The knife cuts only equal pieces; the number of pieces is the bottom number
1. Who's hungry?
one pie, three buddies: the table
is the order (nothing to read)
2. Set the knife
tap the third dot (in VR: twist the
handle, three clicks); no lines yet
3. Slice: equal pieces
one swipe: three equal pieces,
a sparkle and a 'ting'. The cut stays
4. Fair!
one on each plate, ring the bell: the
plates slide and stop side by side
three dots lit: three pieces
all three stop at one third
Not fair yet: four pieces for three
The knife set to four: one piece is left over
(set to two, a buddy has none). Hoot: "Hmm! Not
fair yet." Then: "One piece for each buddy. All
the same size!" The cut pie becomes crumbs for
the robin; a fresh pie comes. A miss costs only
that order's first-time star.
Why the cut stays
A knife with an undo, or lines that show on the pie
before the cut, would let trying every number win:
the model's trial-and-error player then reaches the
bar on 100 % of visits. With the cut final and no
preview, it reaches it on 0 %: the number of pieces
has to be chosen, which is what the bottom number is.
